title: Peter Thiel: You Know Who Else Wants to Regulate AI? The Antichrist
key_facts: Politico's Decoded newsletter (Calder McHugh) obtained recordings of Peter Thiel's first two Nashville lectures in a four-part, $100-per-ticket series.
Politico says the central thesis is that government attempts to regulate AI are evil.
Thiel said Obama and the pope seek popularity by opposing AI, which he called politically unpopular.
Thiel's complaint appears to be Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical, which linked the AI era to "new forms of dehumanization" and an "idolatry of profit that sacrifices the weak".
Thiel claimed the pope used AI as a popular topic to distract from church scandals.
Thiel also criticised effective altruism, saying a one-world government to stop dangerous science would be hard to undo.
Thiel's representatives did not respond to Politico; Gizmodo notes Thiel's wealth is heavily invested in AI.
quote_evidence: “Many people know that AI is politically unpopular, and want to leverage that to boost their own popularity,” Thiel told attendees.
Thiel’s reps didn’t respond to Politico’s request for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: A major AI investor is publicly casting AI regulation as a religious and political evil, in reply to the pope's stance.
event_date: Recordings of the first two Nashville lectures (dates not stated) obtained Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
notes: Politico's original not read; Gizmodo relays it. Gizmodo's tone is openly critical; its opinion lines are kept out of the summary. The pope's encyclical is not dated in the article and we did not carry it.
